mainTopic: When caper buds count as fruit for ערלה and ברכות, and the ברכות on peppers, ginger, and grain-and-honey dishes
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of the caper bush and ערלה outside ארץ ישראל. First the גמרא explains that we may follow רבי עקיבא's lenient view there, but never בית שמאי against בית הלל, because that view is 'not a משנה.' Then it asks why the caper buds (קפריסין) are not forbidden anyway as a שומר לפרי, a covering that protects the fruit. רבא offers three tests for what counts as a שומר. The first two are knocked down by אביי, by a teaching of רב נחמן, and by רב שימי's proof from a משנה about שביעית. רבא's final test is that something is a שומר only if the fruit dies without it, and a real incident with a pomegranate and a caper confirms it. So the halacha follows מר בר רב אשי, who ate the buds, and their ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה. The גמרא then discusses peppers and ginger, concluding that fresh ones count as food while dry ones do not. Finally it rules that a grain dish mixed with honey gets בורא מיני מזונות, based on רב and שמואל, and begins explaining why both versions of their rule are needed, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the quoted משנה on doubtful ערלה outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה. Outside ארץ ישראל, a Jew may buy fruit that might be ערלה from a non-Jew, as long as he does not see it being picked from an ערלה tree. This leniency supports the challenge that we should follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and buy it, as long as he does not see him picking it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a משנה. That quote shows how lenient the rules of ערלה are outside ארץ ישראל, and it is being used to push the challenge: why not follow בית שמאי too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says that doubtful ערלה is forbidden in ארץ ישראל, permitted in סוריא, and outside the Land one may 'go down and buy.' The only limit is that he cannot actually see the fruit picked from an ערלה tree. If even doubtful ערלה is permitted outside the Land, it seems we should rely on the most lenient view, which is בית שמאי's.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
Fruit that might or might not be ערלה
Buys (here: buys the fruit from a non-Jew)
Picks / gathers (the fruit off the tree)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling of the גמרא. It is the tail end of a quoted משנה, and the גמרא uses it as ammunition for the question about בית שמאי.

phrases.english: and buys — provided that he does not see him picking it.
phrases.notes: End of the משנה in ערלה: outside the Land, one may go down to the market and buy doubtful ערלה fruit from a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source quoted earlier as part of the challenge to follow בית שמאי outside the Land.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that outside ארץ ישראל we follow the lenient opinion, which seems to require following בית שמאי as well
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ערלה outside the Land is so lenient that even doubtful fruit may be bought, then the most lenient opinion, בית שמאי's, should be followed.

steps.title: בית שמאי against בית הלל does not count at all
steps.stepSummary: The rule of following the lenient opinion outside the Land only applies to real, valid opinions, like רבי עקיבא against רבי אליעזר. בית שמאי's opinion against בית הלל is treated as if it were never in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי אליעזר, we act like him. But when בית שמאי disagree with בית הלל, it is as if their opinion is not a משנה at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. We follow רבי עקיבא's lenient view, but בית שמאי's view is not a real option to follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following the lenient view outside the Land only works with an opinion that has standing in halacha. רבי עקיבא's view is a valid opinion, so we can rely on it. When בית שמאי argue with בית הלל, the halacha is already fixed like בית הלל, so בית שמאי's view is removed from consideration entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where (someone) argues against (another)
The school of הלל, whose view is the halacha
It is not a משנה, meaning it is treated as nonexistent

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule across all of ש״ס: a view of בית שמאי that opposes בית הלל is not used even as a lenient fallback.
steps.whatToRemember: Leniency outside the Land lets us follow רבי עקיבא, but never בית שמאי against בית הלל, because that view is 'not a משנה.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva where he disagrees with Rabbi Eliezer —
we act according to him;
but Beit Shammai where they disagree with Beit Hillel —
it is not considered a mishna at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּמְקוֹם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר עָבְדִינַן כְּוָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised through the משנה in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule: leniency outside the Land applies only to valid opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any lenient opinion, even בית שמאי's, could be followed outside the Land.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only legitimate opinions like רבי עקיבא's are followed. בית שמאי's view against בית הלל is 'not a משנה.'

steps.title: The קפריסין should be ערלה because they protect the fruit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why do we need the debate at all? The קפריסין protect the fruit (שומר לפרי). The Torah forbids as ערלה whatever is secondary to the fruit, so they should be forbidden anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: But derive it from the fact that it serves as a protection for the fruit. The Torah says, 'You shall treat its fruit as ערלה,' and 'את פריו' means what is secondary to its fruit. What is that? The protection of the fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Even according to רבי עקיבא, the קפריסין should be forbidden as ערלה, because they act as a protective covering for the fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'את' in the פסוק teaches that ערלה includes things attached to the fruit that serve it, such as a protective shell. The קפריסין wrap around the caper berry and protect it. So it seems they should be forbidden no matter whose view we follow.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him derive it (from a simpler reason)
A protective covering of the fruit
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
That which is secondary to its fruit
The outer covering/buds of the caper, as opposed to the berries

steps.confusionAlert: 'וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ' does not mean the גמרא agrees. It is a challenge: 'Why not just use this other, simpler reason?'

phrases.english: But derive it from the fact that it becomes a protection for the fruit,
and the Torah says:
"You shall treat its fruit as orla" (Leviticus 19:23),
'et' includes what is secondary to its fruit,
phrases.notes: The extra word 'את' is read as including things connected to the fruit.

phrases.english: and what is that? The protection of the fruit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from which opinion to follow to a new reason the קפריסין might be forbidden regardless.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling, following רבי עקיבא, that the קפריסין are not ערלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק includes the שומר לפרי in ערלה, and the קפריסין protect the berry, so they should be forbidden.

steps.title: רבא: a covering only counts as protection if it stays on after picking
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that something counts as a שומר לפרי only if it protects the fruit both while attached to the tree and after picking. The קפריסין protect only while attached and fall away once the fruit is picked, so they are not a שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When do we say something is a protection for the fruit? When it is there both when the fruit is picked and when it is attached. Here, it is there while attached, but once picked it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by defining what counts as a שומר לפרי. Because the קפריסין do not stay on the picked fruit, they are not counted as a protective covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא adds a requirement: a real שומר must stay with the fruit in both states, attached and detached. The קפריסין only surround the berry on the plant and come off when it is picked. So the ערלה rule of שומר לפרי does not apply to them, and רבי עקיבא's leniency stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is there / it is not there

steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבא's first of three attempts to define שומר לפרי. Watching each test get rejected shows what the final test (step 14) has to explain.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's first test is that a שומר לפרי must stay on the fruit both on the tree and after picking. Keep this answer in mind only as a first attempt: אביי attacks it in the next step, and רבא replaces it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Where do we say that something becomes a protection for the fruit?

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ בֵּין בְּתָלוּשׁ בֵּין בִּמְחוּבָּר,
phrases.english: Where it is present both when the fruit is detached and when it is attached;
here, when attached — it is present,
when detached — it is not present.
phrases.notes: The covering falls off once the fruit is picked, so it is not a true שומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא הֵיכָא אָמְרִינַן דְּנַעֲשָׂה שׁוֹמֵר לַפְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by narrowing the definition of שומר לפרי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a category more narrowly (adding a condition)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything that protects the fruit at any stage counts as a שומר לפרי and is ערלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a covering that stays with the fruit both attached and detached is a שומר לפרי. The קפריסין are not, since they come off when the fruit is picked.

steps.title: אביי shows that טומאה rules do not decide ערלה
steps.stepSummary: אביי attacks רבא's rule by pointing to the pomegranate flower. It does not count with the fruit for טומאה, yet it is forbidden as ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: a pomegranate's crown counts together with the fruit, but its flower does not. Since the flower does not count, it must not be food. Yet we learned about ערלה that pomegranate peels, the pomegranate flower, nut shells and pits are all forbidden as ערלה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer from Step 4. He shows that something which does not count as part of the fruit for טומאה can still be forbidden as ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא required a שומר to stay with the fruit even after picking. אביי points to the pomegranate's נץ. For טומאה it does not join with the fruit, so it is not treated as part of the picked fruit and is not food. Yet the משנה in ערלה still forbids it. So something can be ערלה even if it is not a lasting part of the picked fruit, which undercuts רבא's requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: The crown (top tip) of a pomegranate
The flower or blossom at the tip of the fruit
Joins together with the fruit to make up the minimum size for טומאה

steps.confusionAlert: The first source (about joining) is about טומאה, not ערלה. אביי puts two different areas of law side by side to show that they do not follow the same rules.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
The crown of a pomegranate joins (for impurity size),
phrases.notes: This source is from the laws of טומאה.

phrases.english: but its flower does not join.
From the fact that it says its flower does not join,
evidently it is not considered food.
And yet we learned regarding orlah:
Pomegranate peels and its flower,
nut shells and the pits
are subject to orlah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's test that a שומר must protect the fruit both while attached and after picking.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pomegranate's נץ is not counted as part of the fruit (it does not join for טומאה), yet it is forbidden as ערלה. So staying with the picked fruit is not required, and the קפריסין could still be forbidden.

steps.title: רבא's new rule: present when the fruit is ripe
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different test. A part counts as a protector only if it is still there when the fruit finishes ripening. The קפריסין fall off before that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: when do we say that something is a protector for the fruit? When it is still there at the time the fruit is fully ripe. This caper bud is no longer there when the fruit is fully ripe.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops his first answer and gives a new reason why the קפריסין are not forbidden as ערלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new test is about timing. Does the covering last until the fruit is finished growing? The קפרס falls away early, so it does not count as a שומר, and it is not forbidden as ערלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals that the earlier answer is dropped)
The completion (full ripening) of the fruit
The caper bud or berry under discussion

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Where do we say
that it becomes a protector for the fruit?
Where it is present when the fruit is fully ripe.
This caper bud
is not present when the fruit is fully ripe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that אביי knocked down in Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New criterion replacing the rejected one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A protector is defined by whether it guards the fruit both attached and detached.
steps.terutzMaskana: A protector is defined by whether it is still there when the fruit is fully ripe. The קפרס is not.

steps.title: Date coverings count as protectors even at an early stage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's new rule. רב נחמן forbids date coverings as ערלה because they protect the fruit, even though they protect it only while it is young.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? Didn't רב נחמן say in the name of רבה בר אבוה: these date coverings of ערלה are forbidden because they became a protector for the fruit. And when do they protect the fruit? Only in its young, early stage. Yet he still calls them 'a protector for the fruit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's new rule by quoting a teaching that calls something a protector even though it is not there when the fruit is ripe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date coverings (מתחלי) cover the date only at its early stage (כופרא), not at full ripeness. Even so, רב נחמן forbids them as a שומר. That goes against רבא's test that a protector must still be there at גמר פירא.

keyTerms.meaning: Coverings or sheaths around young dates
The early, unripe stage of the fruit

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Nachman say in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
These date coverings of orlah are forbidden,
since they became a protector for the fruit.
And when are they a protector for the fruit?
In the early, unripe stage,
and yet he calls it "a protector for the fruit."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's new rule from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that a protector must be present at גמר פירא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Date coverings are there only at the early stage, yet רב נחמן calls them a שומר and forbids them. So being there at full ripeness is not required.

steps.title: רב נחמן follows רבי יוסי, and the רבנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן's teaching follows רבי יוסי, who holds that even a very young grape cluster (סמדר) is already a fruit. The חכמים disagree, so רבא's rule follows the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן holds like רבי יוסי, as we learned: רבי יוסי says the סמדר (budding grape cluster) is forbidden because it is already a fruit. And the חכמים disagree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying that רב נחמן's teaching depends on one side of a מחלוקת, while רבא follows the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, a fruit in its earliest stage is already a real fruit, so whatever covers it at that point is a שומר. The חכמים hold that such an early stage is not yet a fruit. According to them, a covering that is gone before the fruit matures, like the קפרס, is not a protector.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like (follows the opinion of)
A grape cluster at its very first stage, right after the blossoms fall

steps.whatToRemember: This answer ties רבא's ripeness test to the חכמים, who say a very young fruit is not yet a fruit. It is a temporary defense: רב שימי shows in steps 9-13 that this cannot explain the caper bush.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move. Instead of rejecting a source, the גמרא shows that it depends on a מחלוקת, so it does not disprove the other view.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman holds like Rabbi Yosei,
as we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Yosei says:
The budding grape cluster is forbidden
because it is already a fruit.
And the Rabbis disagree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 7 and defends רבא's rule from Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the challenging source to a disputed opinion (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's teaching about date coverings is universally accepted, so it disproves רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן follows רבי יוסי (a young fruit is already a fruit). The חכמים disagree, and רבא's rule follows the חכמים, so the קפריסין are not a שומר.

steps.title: Do the רבנן really argue about other trees?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי מנהרדעא asks whether the רבנן argue with רבי יוסי about trees other than grapevines. He brings a משנה about cutting trees in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי from נהרדעא objected: Do the רבנן argue with רבי יוסי about other trees too? But we learned in a משנה: From when may one no longer cut down trees in the שביעית year? בית שמאי say: all trees, from when they put out fruit. בית הלל say: carob trees, from when they form chains. Vines, from when they reach the גרוע stage. Olive trees, from when they blossom. All other trees, from when they put out fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי attacks the answer from step 8 by asking whether the רבנן's view about young fruit applies to all trees. He brings a משנה that he will use as his ammunition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 used the רבנן to say a young fruit is not yet a fruit, so a cover that protects only the young fruit is not a שומר. רב שימי suspects the רבנן said this only about grapes. The משנה gives vines a special later stage but says all other trees count from the very start.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year (שמיטה); its fruit may not be wasted
From when (the grapes) reach the גרוע stage, explained in the next step

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about שביעית, not ערלה. The גמרא uses it only to learn when the רבנן consider something a 'fruit.' Cutting a tree with fruit on it in שביעית wastes that fruit.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi of Neharde'a objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: וּבִשְׁאָר אִילָנֵי מִי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And regarding other trees, do the Rabbis disagree with him (Rabbi Yosei)?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מֵאֵימָתַי אֵין קוֹצְצִין אֶת הָאִילָנוֹת בַּשְּׁבִיעִית —
phrases.english: From when may one not cut down trees in the Sabbatical year?

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל הָאִילָנוֹת מִשֶּׁיּוֹצִיאוּ,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: all trees, from when they put out fruit;
and Beit Hillel say: carob trees, from when they form chains;
and vines, from when they reach the 'gera' stage;
and olive trees, from when they blossom;
and all other trees, from when they put out fruit.
phrases.notes: This last clause is the key to the challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 8, which tied רבא's rule to the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that the רבנן hold an early-stage fruit is not yet a fruit, and that this explains the קפריסין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the רבנן's view is limited to grapevines, it cannot explain the caper bush. The caper bush is one of the 'other trees,' which count as fruit from the very start.

steps.title: רב אסי defines the גרוע stage of grapes
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי explains that the גרוע stage of vines in the משנה is the בוסר (unripe grape) stage, which he links to a white bean.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אסי said: It (the גרוע stage) is the same as בוסר, it is גרוע, it is a white bean.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי explains the hard word in the משנה (משיגרעו) so the גמרא can work out which opinion the משנה follows. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי says the גרוע stage of the vine is the בוסר stage. That means בית הלל do not forbid cutting a vine at its earliest stage (סמדר). They forbid it only once the grape reaches בוסר. This matches the רבנן in their argument with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: An unripe grape, a stage after the tiny early bud
The grape stage named in the משנה; here identified with בוסר

phrases.english: And Rav Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: הוּא בּוֹסֶר, הוּא גֵּרוּעַ, הוּא פּוֹל הַלָּבָן.
phrases.english: It is an unripe grape, it is 'gera,' it is a white bean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a term in the משנה just quoted, as part of רב שימי's challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משיגרעו in the משנה means the בוסר stage.

steps.title: Can a grape really be a white bean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: how can a grape at any stage be called a white bean?
steps.simpleTranslation: A white bean? Could you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question רב אסי's odd wording. A grape is obviously not a bean. The next step fixes the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a quick question about wording, not an attack on the main argument. It only asks how to read the phrase 'it is a white bean.'

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (expresses surprise at a reading)

phrases.english: A white bean, could it enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of רב אסי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can a grape stage be called a 'white bean'?

steps.title: It means the size of a white bean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the reading: the בוסר stage is reached when the grape is the size of a white bean.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: its size is like a white bean.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב אסי's words. He was giving the size of the grape at this stage, not saying it is a bean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the definition is clear. The grape counts once it reaches בוסר, about the size of a white bean. Before that it does not.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Its size is like a white bean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בוסר stage is when the grape reaches the size of a white bean.

steps.title: Even the רבנן count other trees' fruit from the start
steps.stepSummary: The view 'בוסר yes, סמדר no' belongs to the רבנן. Yet this same משנה says all other trees count from when the fruit first comes out. So the רבנן's view is only about grapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom did you hear say that בוסר counts as fruit but סמדר does not? The רבנן. And yet this משנה teaches that all other trees count from when they put out fruit!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי finishes his challenge. The משנה follows the רבנן, and it shows they treat other trees' fruit as fruit from its very first stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ruling on vines (only from בוסר) matches the רבנן, so the משנה follows the רבנן. But for 'all other trees' it forbids cutting from the first appearance of fruit. So even the רבנן say early fruit of other trees is real fruit. The caper bush is an 'other tree,' so the קפריסין protect a real fruit, and the answer of step 8 fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A tiny early grape bud, before בוסר
Whom have you heard say this? (identifies whose opinion a source follows)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the attempt to tie רבא's rule to the רבנן. That is why the גמרא now needs a completely new explanation.

phrases.english: Whom did you hear who said:
an unripe grape, yes; a grape bud, no?
The Rabbis.
And yet it teaches: all other trees, from when they put out fruit?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר בּוֹסֶר אִין סְמָדַר לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב אסי's definition to complete the challenge begun in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 8, that the רבנן's view explains why the קפריסין are not a שומר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה follows the רבנן, yet it counts the fruit of all non-grape trees from the start. So the רבנן's view cannot help with the caper bush.

steps.title: רבא's new test: does the fruit die without it?
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new rule: something is a שומר only if the fruit dies when it is removed. Removing the caper bud does not kill the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: When do we say something is a שומר for the fruit? When, if you remove that protector, the fruit dies. Here, when you remove it, the fruit does not die.
steps.whatsHappening: Having lost the earlier answer, רבא gives a brand new test for what counts as a שומר. By this test, the קפריסין are not a שומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is no longer about timing (how long it protects or when it falls off). The test is now whether the fruit needs it to survive. The caper fruit survives without its bud, so the bud is not a שומר and is not forbidden as ערלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, רבא said (drops the old approach for a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: Final test: a part of the plant is a שומר לפרי only if the fruit dies without it. So the קפריסין are not a שומר and are not forbidden as ערלה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Where do we say that it is a protector of the fruit?
Where, when you remove the protector,
the fruit dies.
Here, when you remove it,
the fruit does not die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא הֵיכָא אָמְרִינַן דְּהָוֵי שׁוֹמֵר לְפֵרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation knocked down in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New defining criterion (a new rule that replaces the old one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A שומר was defined by how long it protects the fruit, tied to the רבנן's view of young fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שומר is defined by whether the fruit needs it to survive. The caper fruit does not need its bud.

steps.title: A real incident proves the test
steps.stepSummary: Once, people removed a pomegranate's flower and the pomegranate dried up. They removed a caper fruit's flower and the caper survived.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident: they removed the flower of a pomegranate, and the pomegranate withered. They removed the flower of a caper fruit, and the caper fruit survived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's test with a real event. It shows that the pomegranate flower is truly needed, while the caper flower is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This also explains אביי's pomegranate case from step 5. The pomegranate flower is a שומר because the fruit dies without it. The caper bud is not a שומר, because the fruit lives on without it.
steps.whatToRemember: Pomegranate flower: the fruit dies without it, so it is a שומר. Caper bud: the fruit lives without it, so it is not a שומר.

phrases.english: There was an incident
and they removed the flower of a pomegranate,
and the pomegranate withered;
and they removed the flower of a caper fruit,
and the caper fruit survived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's new test from step 14 with a real event.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's test that a שומר is something the fruit cannot survive without.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real incident: the pomegranate died without its flower, but the caper fruit lived without its bud.

steps.title: The halacha follows מר בר רב אשי on capers
steps.stepSummary: The final ruling follows מר בר רב אשי. He threw away the caper berries and ate the caper buds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The halacha is like מר בר רב אשי, who threw away the berries and ate the buds.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the discussion about whether the caper bud 'protects' the fruit, the גמרא gives the final practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא just showed that the caper bud is not a real protector (שומר), because the fruit survives without it. So for ערלה, only the berry (אביונות) is the real fruit, and only it is forbidden. The bud (קפריסין) may be eaten, just as מר בר רב אשי did.

keyTerms.meaning: Caper buds (the outer part, treated as not the real fruit)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling sets up the next line, which uses the ערלה status of capers to decide their ברכה.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Mar bar Rav Ashi
who threw away the berries
phrases.notes: The berries are the real fruit and are forbidden as ערלה.

phrases.english: and ate the buds
phrases.notes: The buds are not the fruit, so ערלה does not apply to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבא's rule and the story of the pomegranate and caper into a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Caper buds are not 'fruit' for ערלה. Only the berries are.

steps.title: Caper buds get the blessing of fruit of the ground
steps.stepSummary: Since caper buds are not 'fruit' for ערלה, they are not 'fruit' for ברכות either. Their ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה, not בורא פרי העץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since they are not fruit for ערלה, they are also not fruit for ברכות. So we do not say בורא פרי העץ on them, but בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the ערלה ruling to our topic of ברכות and decides what ברכה to say on caper buds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that one definition of 'fruit of the tree' works for both areas of halacha. If the bud is not the tree's real fruit for ערלה, it cannot be 'fruit of the tree' for a ברכה either. It still grows from the ground, so it gets בורא פרי האדמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
The ברכה on fruit of a tree
The ברכה on produce of the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Caper buds are not 'tree fruit,' either for ערלה or for ברכות. Their ברכה is בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean capers are a ground vegetable. The bud grows on a tree, but it is not that tree's true fruit, so it gets the general ground ברכה.

phrases.english: And since regarding orla they are not fruit

phrases.aramaic: לְגַבֵּי בְּרָכוֹת נָמֵי לָאו פֵּירָא נִינְהוּ,
phrases.english: regarding blessings they are also not fruit
and we do not recite over it 'Who creates fruit of the tree'
but rather 'Who creates fruit of the ground'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the ערלה ruling and applies it to ברכות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברכה on caper buds is בורא פרי האדמה.

steps.title: What blessing is said on peppers
steps.stepSummary: A new topic. רב ששת says the ברכה on peppers is שהכל. רבא says no ברכה is said at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Peppers: רב ששת said you say שהכל. רבא said you say nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the ברכה on peppers. It brings two opposite opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת holds that peppers count as food, but only enough for the general ברכה of שהכל. רבא holds that peppers are not food at all, because people do not normally eat sharp spices on their own. So he says no ברכה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The general ברכה: 'by Whose word all things came to be'

phrases.english: Peppers: Rav Sheshet said: 'shehakol'
Rava said: nothing at all

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from capers to another unusual food, peppers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת: say שהכל on peppers. רבא: no ברכה at all.

steps.title: רבא is consistent with his יום כיפור ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבא's view fits his other ruling: someone who chews peppers or ginger on יום כיפור is exempt, because that is not 'eating.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא follows his own reasoning, because רבא said: someone who chews peppers on יום כיפור is exempt, and someone who chews ginger on יום כיפור is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבא's 'no ברכה' opinion matches another ruling of his about יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור, you are only liable for real eating. רבא says chewing peppers or ginger does not count, so peppers are not 'food' in his eyes. For the same reason, they need no ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (he is consistent)

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own reasoning, as Rava said:
one who chews peppers on Yom Kippur is exempt
one who chews ginger on Yom Kippur is exempt

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's view from the previous step with another ruling of his.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that peppers need no ברכה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling that chewing peppers or ginger on יום כיפור is not 'eating'

steps.title: רבי מאיר includes peppers in ערלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא challenges רבא. רבי מאיר learns from the words 'עץ מאכל' that the pepper tree, whose wood and fruit taste the same, is subject to ערלה. That shows peppers are food, and it shows that ארץ ישראל lacks nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised. רבי מאיר would say: From the words 'you shall treat its fruit as ערלה,' don't I already know it is a food tree? So why does the verse say 'a food tree'? To include a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same. Which tree is that? Pepper. This teaches that peppers are subject to ערלה, and that ארץ ישראל lacks nothing, as it says: 'A land where you will eat bread without poverty; you will lack nothing in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא with a ברייתא that treats peppers as a real food tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says the extra words 'עץ מאכל' come to include the pepper tree. So the Torah counts peppers as food, and they are forbidden as ערלה. That contradicts רבא, who said peppers are not food at all, both for יום כיפור and for ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
Its wood and its fruit taste the same

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Meir would say:
From the implication of what is said, 'you shall treat its fruit as orla'
don't I know that it is a food tree?
Rather, why does the verse say 'a food tree'?

phrases.aramaic: לְהָבִיא עֵץ שֶׁטַּעַם עֵצוֹ וּפִרְיוֹ שָׁוֶה,
phrases.english: To include a tree whose wood and fruit taste the same
And which is it? This is the pepper tree
to teach you that peppers are subject to orla

phrases.aramaic: וּלְלַמֶּדְךָ שֶׁאֵין אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל חֲסֵרָה כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: and to teach you that the Land of Israel lacks nothing
as it is said: 'A land in which, without poverty'
you will eat bread in it
you will lack nothing in it'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's view that peppers are not food.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that peppers are not food and need no ברכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Torah calls the pepper tree an עץ מאכל for ערלה, then peppers must be real food.

steps.title: Fresh peppers versus dry peppers
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that there is no contradiction. רבי מאיר is talking about fresh, moist peppers, which are food. רבא is talking about dry peppers, which are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about fresh peppers, and that one is about dry peppers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that each source is talking about a different kind of pepper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh peppers can actually be eaten, so the Torah includes them in ערלה. Dry peppers are too sharp to eat on their own, so chewing them is not 'eating' on יום כיפור and needs no ברכה. רבא's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: Fresh peppers count as food. Dry peppers do not, so according to רבא they need no ברכה and do not break the fast on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this is about fresh ones
and this is about dry ones

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּרַטִּיבְתָּא, הָא בְּיַבִּשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): fresh versus dry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי מאיר and רבא disagree about whether peppers are food.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fresh peppers are food and are subject to ערלה. Dry peppers are not food for יום כיפור or for ברכות.

steps.title: The רבנן challenge the ruling that chewing ginger on יום כיפור is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask מרימר: how can chewing ginger on יום כיפור be exempt? רבא said Indian ginger is permitted and gets בורא פרי האדמה, so it counts as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to מרימר: Is someone who chews ginger on יום כיפור really exempt? But רבא said: Ginger that comes from India is permitted, and we say בורא פרי האדמה over it!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן raise a contradiction. If ginger gets a food ברכה, it should count as eating on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 we learned that chewing pepper or ginger on יום כיפור is not 'eating.' But רבא himself treats ginger as a real food, since it gets a ברכה and is permitted to eat. Both rulings cannot be true about the same ginger.
steps.confusionAlert: Two different words for ginger appear here (זנגבילא and המלתא). They mean the same thing. The challenge only works because both refer to ginger.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Mareimar:
One who chews ginger on Yom Kippur is exempt?
But didn't Rava say:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי הִמְלְתָא דְּאָתְיָא מִבֵּי הִנְדּוּאֵי — שַׁרְיָא,
phrases.english: This ginger that comes from India is permitted,
phrases.notes: רש״י: we are not worried about how non-Jews prepared it.

phrases.english: and we recite over it 'Who creates fruit of the ground.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of food-versus-not-food contradiction from steps 20 and 21, now to ginger.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one who chews ginger on יום כיפור is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא gives ginger a food ברכה (בורא פרי האדמה), so ginger is food. Eating food on יום כיפור should make a person liable.

steps.title: Fresh ginger is food, dry ginger is not
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. The ברכה ruling is about fresh, moist ginger. The יום כיפור exemption is about dry ginger.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is about moist ginger, and that ruling is about dry ginger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge the same way it answered about peppers in step 21: moist versus dry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh ginger is eaten as food, so it gets בורא פרי האדמה and would count as eating on יום כיפור. Dry ginger is only a spice, so chewing it is not eating. Each ruling is about a different form of ginger.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: For both pepper and ginger, fresh is treated as food: it gets a ברכה and counts as eating. Dry is not food: no ברכה, and chewing it on יום כיפור is exempt.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is about moist ginger, that is about dry ginger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling applies to a different state of the food.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ginger is one category, so its ברכה law and its יום כיפור law should match.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist ginger is food (ברכה, liable on יום כיפור). Dry ginger is not food (exempt on יום כיפור).

steps.title: A dispute about the blessing on a grain-and-honey dish
steps.stepSummary: New topic. For חביץ קדרה and דייסא, רב יהודה says the ברכה is שהכל נהיה בדברו. רב כהנא says it is בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: About חביץ קדרה (a pot dish of flour, oil and honey), and likewise דייסא (pounded grain): רב יהודה said the ברכה is 'שהכל נהיה בדברו.' רב כהנא said it is 'בורא מיני מזונות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a two-sided disagreement about which ברכה to say on a grain dish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both dishes are made from grain, but other ingredients are mixed in. רב יהודה gives the general ברכה (שהכל). רב כהנא gives the grain-food ברכה (בורא מיני מזונות). The next step explains exactly where they disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: a pot-cooked dish of flour, oil and honey
'By Whose word all things came to be' (the general ברכה)
'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment' (ברכה for grain foods)

phrases.english: Pot-cooked ḥavitz, and likewise pounded grain:
Rav Yehuda said: 'By Whose word all things came to be.'
Rav Kahana said: 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. It continues the daf's larger theme of which ברכה fits which food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: שהכל. רב כהנא: בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: Defining exactly where רב יהודה and רב כהנא disagree
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that plain דייסא gets בורא מיני מזונות. They only argue about דייסא cooked with honey like חביץ קדרה. רב יהודה holds the honey is the main part. רב כהנא holds the flour is the main part.
steps.simpleTranslation: For plain pounded grain, everyone agrees the ברכה is 'בורא מיני מזונות.' They argue about pounded grain made like חביץ קדרה. רב יהודה says 'שהכל' because he holds the honey is the main part. רב כהנא says 'בורא מיני מזונות' because he holds the flour is the main part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the argument and explains the reasoning behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step first removes plain grain from the argument, since that is simply בורא מיני מזונות. The real question is a mixture: which ingredient is the עיקר (main part)? The ברכה goes on the main ingredient. Honey gets שהכל, and grain gets בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה does not say grain is שהכל. He agrees plain grain is בורא מיני מזונות. He only says that in this sweet mixture the honey is the main part.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of עיקר (main ingredient) decides the ברכה is the key to all the mixture questions that follow.

phrases.english: With plain pounded grain alone,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּ״בוֹרֵא מִינֵי מְזוֹנוֹת״.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that it is 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּדַיְיסָא כְּעֵין חֲבִיץ קְדֵרָה,
phrases.english: Where they argue is pounded grain made like pot-cooked ḥavitz:
Rav Yehuda said 'all things,'
because he holds that the honey is the main part.
Rav Kahana said 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment,'
because he holds that the flour is the main part.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תשובה (an explanation of the scope of the dispute)
steps.triggerLanguage: בְּדַיְיסָא גְּרֵידָא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute of step 24 and gives each side's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plain דייסא is agreed to be בורא מיני מזונות. In a honey mixture, the ברכה follows whichever ingredient is the עיקר, and that is the point of dispute.

steps.title: רב יוסף supports רב כהנא from a rule of רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רב כהנא's view makes sense. רב ושמואל both said that anything containing one of the five grains gets בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב כהנא's view is more reasonable. רב ושמואל both said: anything that has any of the five grains in it gets the ברכה 'בורא מיני מזונות.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings support from an earlier authority to decide the argument in favor of רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל say that grain in a dish makes it בורא מיני מזונות, even when other ingredients are mixed in. That means the grain counts as the main part, which is רב כהנא's reasoning. Honey does not cancel out the grain.

keyTerms.meaning: the five grains (wheat, barley, spelt, oats, rye)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: a dish with real grain content from the חמשת המינין gets בורא מיני מזונות.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is reasonable to rule like Rav Kahana,
since Rav and Shmuel both said:
Anything that has in it any of the five species of grain,
we recite over it 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute of step 25 in favor of רב כהנא.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's view that the grain is the main part, so the ברכה is בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב ושמואל: anything containing one of the five grains gets בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: Quoting רב and שמואל's rule in its two versions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב ושמואל's rule again ('anything that HAS the five grains IN it'). It notes that another version was also reported ('anything that IS FROM the five grains'). This raises the question of why both were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the main statement itself. רב ושמואל both said: anything that has any of the five grains in it gets 'בורא מיני מזונות.' It was also reported that רב ושמואל both said: anything that is made from the five grains gets 'בורא מיני מזונות.'
steps.whatsHappening: With the word 'גופא' the גמרא goes back to examine רב ושמואל's statement on its own. It places the two versions side by side, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions look almost the same, so one of them seems unnecessary. The difference is in the wording: 'has IN it' points to mixtures, while 'IS FROM' points to the grain itself. The next step explains why both statements were needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': returning to analyze a statement quoted earlier
anything that has in it (a mixture)
anything that is (from the grain itself)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a pointless repeat. The גמרא quotes the rule again on purpose, to compare the two versions and show that each teaches something.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav and Shmuel both said:
Anything that has in it any of the five species,
we recite over it 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'
And it was also stated:
Rav and Shmuel both said:
Anything that is from the five species,
we recite over it 'Who creates the various kinds of nourishment.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (an implied question of why both statements are needed)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the source cited as proof in step 26 and studies it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ושמואל taught both 'כל שיש בו' and 'כל שהוא' from the five grains get בורא מיני מזונות.

steps.title: Why both versions are needed: the first half of the explanation
steps.stepSummary: Both statements are necessary. If we only had 'כל שהוא,' we would think בורא מיני מזונות applies only to pure grain and not to mixtures. The other half of the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both statements are needed. If they had only taught 'anything that IS from the five grains,' I would have thought that rule applies because the grain is in its pure form. But in a mixture, I would think the ברכה is not בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to show that neither version is extra. This passage gives the first half: why the 'mixture' version is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כל שהוא' alone could be read as covering only plain, unmixed grain. The second statement, 'כל שיש בו,' teaches that grain in a mixture also gets בורא מיני מזונות. The reverse half (why 'כל שהוא' is needed) comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: it is necessary (both statements are needed)

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for if he had taught us only 'anything that is,'
I would have said
that it is because the grain is in its pure form,
but in a mixture, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question of step 27: why were both versions needed?
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something the other does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From 'כל שהוא' alone, one would think only pure grain gets בורא מיני מזונות and mixtures do not.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל שיש בו' is needed to teach that grain in a mixture also gets בורא מיני מזונות. The reverse side continues on the next amud.
